overview.time_sub: {plays} plays · {artists} artists · {tracks} tracks · {avg} on average per play

tops.title: Top charts
tops.no_genre: No genre known yet (enrichment runs in the background).
tops.unknown_genre: {n} plays without a known genre are not counted.
tops.lead: Your favorite artists, albums, tracks and genres, ranked by plays or by minutes.
tops.hero_lead: Leading: {artist} ({value}). Most played album: {album}. Top track: {track}.
tops.artists_note: Colours follow each artist's main genre.
tops.albums_note: Each cover's area is proportional to its listening.
tops.genres_note: Genres and the artists behind them.
tops.tables_note: Full tables, sortable, exportable to Excel or CSV.
tops.genre_covers_note: With the album that carries each genre.
tops.wheel_hint: click: dive in · click the centre: back
tops.wheel_note: Genres, then artists, then albums: click a genre or an artist to dive in, the centre to come back. Hover to see the photo or the cover.

evolution.title: Trends
evolution.share_note: The period's top 3 genres and artists; everything else is grouped under "Other".
evolution.lead: How your listening changes over time, and the share of the genres and artists that matter.

habits.title: Listening habits
habits.skip_threshold_help: A play shorter than this counts as skipped.
habits.skip_rate_help: Share of plays shorter than {s} s (whole period, ignoring the minimum-duration filter).
habits.no_skips: No skipped track in this period.
habits.lead: When you listen, how many days in a row, and what you skip the fastest.

discoveries.title: Discoveries
discoveries.since_note: "New" = first play recorded by the app (earlier history is not imported).
discoveries.lead: The artists and albums that entered your musical life, month after month.
discoveries.hero_lead: {artists} artists and {albums} albums heard for the first time, {share} of your listening.
discoveries.swarm_note: Each bubble is an artist, placed on the day you first played them; its size is how much you listened since, its colour its genre.
discoveries.growth_note: Total artists and albums heard at least once.
discoveries.split_note: Each square is 0.5% of your listening time.
discoveries.timeline_note: Each cover is a discovery, placed on the day, week or month of its first play; the most played since sit at the bottom. Hover a cover for its name.

detail.artist_lead: Main genre: {genre}. {plays} plays, {time} in total, since {date}.

history.title: History
history.lead: Every timestamped play, searchable and exportable.
history.hero_lead: {n} plays in the period, {time} of music.

wrapped.title: Recap
wrapped.share_hint: To share this recap, copy the page address: it contains the period and the language.
wrapped.fact_hour_cap: the hour you start the most tracks

admin.title: Corrections
admin.subtitle: The only page that writes to the database. Corrections apply to statistics without touching raw data.
admin.no_password: ADMIN_PASSWORD is not set: this page is disabled.
admin.merge_artists_help: All plays of the first artist will count for the second one.
admin.merge_albums_help: All plays of the first album will count for the second one.
admin.hide_help: A hidden play disappears from stats and history (it stays in the database).
admin.read_only: The hosted site reads a copy of the database: make corrections from the app on your computer; they are published at the next refresh.

library.title: Favorite albums & playlists
library.subtitle: Your Deezer library, cross-checked with your listening history.
library.empty: Library not loaded yet: run a sync (`python -m scripts.sync --library`).
library.listened_share_help: Share of favorite albums with at least one track in your recorded history.
library.added_per_month: Albums added to favorites per month
library.creator: Created by
library.played_share_help: Share of the playlist's tracks found at least once in your history.
library.pick_playlist: Click a playlist to see its tracks.
library.excel_help: One workbook with three sheets: favorite albums, playlists, and every track of each playlist (with your plays).
library.poster_title: A3 poster of my favorite albums
library.poster_help: A blank A3 landscape page (PDF) with every cover in a grid; under each: album title, release date, artist. Sizes adapt so that everything fits.
library.poster_layout: {n} albums → {cols} columns × {rows} rows grid, covers about {size} mm wide.
library.listened_share_short: at least one track in the history
library.hero_lead: {albums} favourite albums by {artists} artists and {playlists} playlists, analysed, exportable to Excel or as an A3 poster.
library.decade_note: Above each decade, your most played favourite album.

explore.title: Explorations
explore.lead: Your listening seen differently: as a spiral, an orbit, a constellation and a fingerprint.
explore.spiral_help: Time winds out from the centre; the angle is the time of day. Dot size follows the time listened, colour the genre. Hover a dot to see the track.
explore.orbit_kicker: Your albums on a golden spiral
explore.orbit_help: The most played albums are the biggest. Hover a cover to see its name.
explore.constellation_help: Each territory is a genre; inside, each glowing cloud gathers one artist's plays. Hover a cloud to see who it is, zoom with the wheel to enter a territory: every name appears.
explore.fingerprint_help: One ring per hour of the day, midnight in the centre, 11 pm outside. The more you listen at that hour, the more the ring waves; its colour is the dominant genre. Every period gives a unique print.
explore.hero_lead: {plays} plays, {artists} artists, {genres} genres: your music, drawn differently.
explore.fingerprint_story: A one-of-a-kind print: one ring per hour of the day, midnight at the centre, 11 pm at the edge. The more you listen at that hour, the more the ring ripples; its colour is the leading genre. Download it, print it, share it.
explore.zoom_hint: wheel or pinch: zoom · drag: move · double-click: reset

refresh.up_to_date: Already up to date: no new play.

home.title: Your listening
home.lead: {time} of music, {share} of it with {artist}. Your biggest day: {day} ({day_time}).
home.bar_colour_note: Each bar wears the colour of its main genre.

rhythms.lead: You mostly listen on {day}s, around {hour}. Current streak: {streak} days (record: {best}).
rhythms.streak_cap: days in a row with at least one play
rhythms.time_note: Each bar takes a deeper colour when you listened more.
rhythms.bars_note: From yellow (little) to violet (a lot); above, the most played album.
rhythms.bump_note: The rank of your top 6, period after period (top = no. 1).
rhythms.too_short: Pick a longer period to see a change.
rhythms.stream_note: Each genre's share of your listening.
rhythms.week_note: When the music plays, day by day and hour by hour.
rhythms.matrix_note: Size = amount, colour = time of day (violet night, golden morning, blue evening).
rhythms.skip_rate_cap: stopped before the end, at any moment
rhythms.week_covers_note: For each day and hour, the most played album; the bigger, the more you listened. The ring gives the time of day.
rhythms.skip_note: A track counts as skipped as soon as it stops before the end, even very early. Deezer only lists plays of about 30 s or more in its history: faster skips are not in it.

reco.lead: {n} tracks you have never played, picked from {artists}, your genres ({genres}) and what you play {moment}. Click a cover to hear 30 s.
reco.empty: Not enough plays in this period to recommend anything yet: pick a longer period.
reco.unavailable: Deezer cannot be reached right now: try again in a moment.
reco.loading: The three engines are searching for you…
reco.tile_neighbours: new artists close to your {n} favourites
reco.map_note: Each territory is one of your genres. White discs are your artists; around them, what each engine suggests, linked to the music it comes from.
reco.map_hint: wheel or pinch: zoom · drag: move · click a cover: listen
reco.how_neighbours: For each of your favourite artists, Deezer knows about twenty artists that sound alike. A neighbour ranks higher the more you play its starting artist and the closer it is; for big batches the graph is walked one step further. One key track per new artist.
reco.how_genres: We read the 300 top tracks of Deezer's charts in each of your genres, then share them out by the place each genre takes in your listening. Only artists new to you, one track each.
reco.how_moment: We play the Deezer radio of the artists you play most {moment}, to fit the time of day. Artists you do not know yet come first, each only once.
reco.none: This engine found nothing new for now.
reco.footnote: 30 s previews provided by Deezer, requested when you click. Nothing already in your history is suggested.
reco.studio_lead: Pick a mode and how many tracks to discover, then generate. Everything starts from your listening (including {artists}) and nothing you have already played comes back. Each mode keeps its latest results until you generate it again.
reco.estimate: for {n} tracks · about {calls} requests to Deezer, which accepts about ten per second
reco.keep_note: This mode's results are kept until the next generation.
reco.empty_hint: Choose how many tracks above and generate.
reco.map_note_mode: Each territory is one of your genres. White discs are your artists; around them, the “{mode}” tracks, linked to the music they come from. Click a cover to hear 30 s.
reco.table_note: Click a cover to hear 30 s, a header to sort, or type a few letters to filter.
reco.step_graph2: Walking one step further in the artist graph…
reco.step_tracks: Picking a key track for each new artist…
